Doubt Clarification

Additional practice
Mock tests
Revision
Continuous guidance

Why the Refund Was Declined

The refund request was received 8th month after admission, after the student had already undergone the core course and had continuous access to the academy's resources.

The duration of enrollment.
Completion of the core learning period.
Continuous access to course materials and support.
The academy's refund policy, which was applied consistently.
A Respectful Clarification

We understand and genuinely sympathize with the student's financial situation and work commitments.

However, personal circumstances cannot change the fact that the course had already been delivered over several months before the refund request was made.

We remain committed to treating every student fairly, consistently, and transparently.

This college, located in the thriving area of Kilpauk on Poonamallee High Road. It is renowned for its extensive medical education programs and comprehensive healthcare facilities.

Over the years, it has grown to include a wide spectrum of undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma, and super-speciality courses, with MBBS being its flagship program. Admissions are conducted via national competitive exams, ensuring a merit-based intake of students from across India.

The campus itself stretches across eight acres, providing an environment that balances the academic intensity of medical studies with the needs of students’ daily lives. The infrastructure features a blend of legacy buildings and newer state-of-the-art facilities, including lecture halls, a central library, research laboratories, sports areas, and separate hostels for men and women.

An impressive highlight is the modern multi-speciality hospital block, which supports advanced medical departments such as neurology, cardiology, emergency care, nephrology, plastic surgery, and trauma management.

Kilpauk Medical College’s affiliation with The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University reflects its commitment to upholding regional and national medical standards. The institution is approved by the Medical Council of India and National Medical Commission, and it has steadily cultivated a reputation for producing highly competent medical professionals.

Faculty members are widely respected and bring a wealth of experience to their teaching, ensuring that students receive instruction that is both rigorous and compassionate.

The institution’s attached hospitals collectively contribute to its dual mission of education and patient care, serving a steadily growing number of patients and providing practical training for students.

The emergency departments in particular are recognized for their adherence to modern protocols, including zero-delay wards for immediate medical intervention.

Notable alumni from Kilpauk Medical College have made significant contributions in medical fields across India, furthering the legacy of the college as a center for excellence in healthcare and research.

This letter serves as official feedback from the Apoøllo Academy of Yoga (Kundrathur) regarding the 3rd State Level Yoga Championship held recently at your K K Nagar West campus.

As a reputed academy, we registered 26 of our students (ranging from 5 to 47 years old, including two special needs children) well in advance. We completed our registration and paid the Rs. 13,000 fee 10 days prior to the event, operating under the assumption that a program hosted by a respected college would be highly professional and well-organized.

Unfortunately, the reality was deeply disappointing. The event was severely mismanaged, and we wish to place the following points on record:

1.	Logistical and Scheduling Failures

No Parking Facilities:
There was absolutely no organized car parking. When asked, your staff dismissively told us to “park anywhere,” completely washing their hands of the responsibility.

Severe Delays & Poor Time Management:
We were instructed to report by 7:30 AM for an 8:00 AM start. Instead, we were met with an unexpected, secondary registration process just to allocate “Chest Numbers.”

Spot Registration Chaos: The chest number allocation was severely delayed (over an hour) because the organizing team prioritized unlimited, on-the-spot registrations over pre-registered institutions.

Shortage of Materials: Due to the greed of accepting unlimited spot registrations, the organizers actually ran out of certificates. Our students were forced to wait indefinitely for reprints.

2.	Lack of Basic Amenities and Communication

No Food or Water: Despite the substantial entry fees, there was absolutely no provision for food or even basic drinking water from 7:30 AM to 3:00 PM. Participants, including young children, were left to struggle.

Denial of Coach Access:
We were initially assured that coaches could accompany their participants. This rule was suddenly reversed on the ground, leaving both parents and coaches entirely clueless about the whereabouts and progress of their students.

Absence of Recognition:
There was zero acknowledgment or recognition given to the participating centers and institutions who brought in the bulk of your competitors.

3.	Unfair Judging and Favoritism

Blatant Favoritism: The organizing team gave clear, visible priority to certain centers. When this was directly pointed out to the organizers, we received absolutely no response.

Jury Bias:
We witnessed juries actively influencing each other to favor their own students. This deeply disappointed and demoralized genuine, hard-working talents.

Mishandling of Special Needs Children:
We brought two special needs children and had intimated the organizers in advance. Despite this, they were judged by the juries in the “normal” category. Because the juries were understaffed and overwhelmed by the massive crowd, they were entirely unable to concentrate on or accurately evaluate real talent.

4.	Unaccountable Leadership

Missing Organizers:
Mr. Annadurai and Mr. Badhri were highly responsive and showed great interest when it came to collecting registration details and money initially. However, on the day of the event, when real leadership and problem-solving were required, both were completely untraceable.

Conclusion
Our overall experience indicates a severe lack of organizational skill. It is incredibly disheartening to say that this event did not feel driven by a passion for Yoga or the development of students. Instead, the unlimited spot registrations, lack of basic amenities, and biased judging made it feel entirely like a money-making scam.
